subject: physics
title: Capacitance Defined: C = Q / V
welcome_lead: Store charge per volt and meet the farad — a surprisingly huge unit.
meta_desc: A-Level Capacitance adventure on definition of capacitance and parallel-plate basics.
final_note: Capacitance is geometry: bigger plates, smaller gap and a good dielectric all help.

concepts.def: Device storing energy in an electric field.
Charge stored per volt: C = Q / V.
Coulomb per volt; 1 F is very large.

walkthroughs.body_html: A capacitor's capacitance is the charge stored per volt across its terminals. C in farads, Q in coulombs, V in volts. Most practical caps are µF, nF or pF.
C = ε₀ ε_r A / d. Larger area or smaller separation increases C. A dielectric of permittivity ε_r boosts C by ε_r compared with vacuum.
Connecting to a battery moves charge until V_cap = V_supply. Then Q = CV. No further current flows in DC steady state.

mcqs.q: Why is the electric field between parallel charged plates considered uniform?
options: Because the plates are uniform in shape.
There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Field strength is constant in magnitude and direction throughout the region (away from edges), unlike the inverse-square field of a point charge.
The field still decreases with the inverse square of distance — uniform just means it's smooth.

mcqs.q: In which direction does an electric field point near a positive charge?
options: There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Radially outwards — the field is defined by the force on a positive test charge, which is repelled.
Because the plates are uniform in shape.
Radially inwards because positive attracts negative.

mcqs.q: What does gravitational field strength at a point represent?
options: The mass of the object creating the field.
There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
The force per unit mass that would act on a test mass placed at that point.
The total gravitational force at that point regardless of mass.

sequence.def: Switch closes; emf starts to drive electrons round
Electrons pile onto one plate and leave the other
Q rises and V = Q/C grows across the plates
Plate pd opposes the emf; I falls exponentially
Capacitor pd equals supply emf; current is zero
